**OpenAI may move forward with new business structure, partnership with Microsoft, regulators say**
OpenAI has restructured its ownership by converting its business into a public benefit corporation, with the Delaware and California attorneys general stating they would not oppose the move, effectively ending over a year of regulatory negotiations. The company, founded in 2015 as a nonprofit with a mission to safely develop artificial general intelligence (AGI), now operates under a new structure where a nonprofit entity—the OpenAI Foundation—retains control over the for-profit public benefit corporation. The nonprofit holds a $130 billion stake, while Microsoft holds a 27% stake valued at $135 billion. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman stated the most likely path forward is an initial public offering (IPO), though no formal announcement was made. **OpenAI Reorganizes Ownership Structure, Becomes Public-Benefit Corporation**
OpenAI restructured its ownership model on October 28, 2025, converting its business into a public-benefit corporation, with approval from Delaware's Attorney General Kathy Jennings, who stated she did not oppose the plan, effectively ending over a year of negotiations. The reorganization allows OpenAI to generate profits more easily while remaining technically under the control of a non-profit entity.
